speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech problems. To understand what is happening, could you tell me how long these symptoms have been getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The combination of progressive gait failure, urinary incontinence, and bulbar symptoms (speech slurring) over a three-month period is highly suggestive of a rapidly progressive motor neuron disease. Given the urgency, I must confirm the diagnosis with immediate testing.
